proposal.summary: USB inspection succeeds showing the phone is inspectable, while Wi-Fi shows the TV transport is reachable without granting relay access. BLE shows no fresh observation through the TV and the earlier phone relay observation is stale, coinciding with TV relay readiness reporting nearby-device permission unavailable where the exact dialog has not been inspected. These are synthetic observations to be kept separate from unverified possible causes, motivating ordered read-only owner review.

hypotheses.explanation: Observation is that TV Wi-Fi reachability coexists with unavailable nearby-device permission and absence of fresh BLE relay data, while USB proves the phone remains inspectable. One unverified possible cause is that the unavailable permission state prevents relay readiness, which would explain why network reachability does not produce relay access. This keeps observed transport states distinct from the hypothesized permission block and does not claim a confirmed cause.

Observation is that the only phone relay evidence is stale and an earlier observation exists without fresh TV BLE data to replace it. Another unverified possible cause is evidence ageing or timing gap rather than device incapability, meaning stale data could be misread as current absence if age is not compared. This distinguishes the observed staleness from inferences about present relay ability and does not claim confirmation.

checks.reason: Owner reads the TV permission state on its own screen in a read-only manner to clarify the reported unavailable nearby-device permission, since the exact dialog has not been inspected. This is first because later readiness review depends on knowing what was actually shown, without changing any setting.

Owner reviews current relay readiness after the permission inspection to see whether readiness remains unavailable in light of the confirmed screen state, without starting a scan. Ordering after inspect_permission ensures interpretation uses observed permission state rather than assuming cause, preserving read-only distinction between observation and possible cause.

Owner compares phone relay evidence age in read-only review, explicitly treating stale earlier observation as non-current to avoid conflating past with present. This complements TV-side checks by clarifying what USB inspection proves versus what fresh relay would require, without performing any repair or permission change.
